clue.text: Endless series of notes written by one, a Shakespeare character

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the following word is cut off

blocks.note: an octave is a run of eight notes on a scale
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician scribbles a run of notes, apparently in the hand of some figure from Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: OCTAVE loses its last letter, then I and A follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavia is the sister of Octavius Caesar and wife of Mark Antony in Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Reversed more than is usual, then changed direction

blocks.note: over as in overdone, beyond the normal amount
to turn is to change direction

explanation.surface: Someone backtracked more than usual and then swung off another way.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision overturned on appeal has been reversed, undone by a higher authority.

clue.text: Hackneyed yarn, unembellished?

blocks.note: yarn is spun thread
bare means plain, with no ornament

explanation.surface: A worn-out story told plainly, with yarn in its sense of a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' reads as a story, which fits 'hackneyed', but here it is the thread for knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A threadbare argument or joke is worn out through overuse, just as hackneyed means stale and trite.

clue.text: Receiving repair, damaged plant

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are put back in a new order

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A damaged plant is being taken in for repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a North American climbing vine grown on walls for its red autumn leaves.

clue.text: Notice fit little boy getting changed

blocks.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
apt means suitable
Ed is a short form of Edward, a boy's name made little

explanation.surface: Look: a healthy young lad is changing his clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adapted has been modified to suit new conditions, a synonym for altered.

clue.text: Unfair arrangement that involves untreated wood

blocks.note: raw means unprocessed
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A timber merchant complains that the contract involves wood that has not been treated.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a name for softwood planks, a sense many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is idiomatic for harsh or unjust treatment, a bargain that leaves someone worse off.

clue.text: No regrets?

blocks.note: surface reading: a carefree life with nothing to be sorry about
setter's reading: 'No' and 'regrets', as in a polite reply to an invitation, are both ways of declining

explanation.walkthrough: 'Regrets' is the formal word on a card sent back to decline an invitation, and 'No' is the blunt version; both are the same kind of reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A refusal is a declining of an offer or request, which is exactly what both 'no' and 'regrets' convey.

clue.text: Western fancy goods they had in plant

indicators.note: as a verb, fancy means imagine or invent, so the letters are refashioned freely

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for western
the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Cowboys imported fine goods into the plant, or so it reads.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody nightshade, also called bittersweet, is a poisonous scrambling plant of the potato family.

clue.text: Leave former partner with it

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to walk away from an old flame, taking it along.
explanation.definitionFit: To exit is to go out or depart, the verb sense matching leave.

clue.text: Guide boy round centre of Crewe

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, so only that one is kept
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
the middle letter of the town name; Crewe is an English railway town

explanation.surface: A lad leads someone around the middle of Crewe, a town in Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead is to show the way or direct, a verb synonym of guide.

clue.text: Terribly irate going round ancient city in ancient country

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the next word is jumbled
to go round something is to encircle it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An angry crowd surrounds an old city somewhere in the ancient world.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was the land of the Etruscans in central Italy before Roman dominance.

clue.text: Woman ringing daughter on island state

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the name goes around what follows
placed on means added after, so the piece before this word is sent second

blocks.note: Flora is a woman's name
I is the abbreviation for island
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A woman phones her daughter, who is living on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daughter on island' puts D after I, giving ID, which goes inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Florida is a state of the USA, the peninsula in the south-east.

clue.text: So tasty, Thai cooking in other words

indicators.note: cooking mixes and transforms ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A diner praises Thai food as delicious, putting it another way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a restatement or clarification of what was just said, meaning namely.

clue.text: Troublesome lout ain't as welcome

indicators.note: something troublesome causes disorder, so the following letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
also part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A troublemaker grumbles that he isn't welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A salutation is a greeting, the noun sense of welcome as a friendly reception.

clue.text: Ted Heath was one reportedly suppressed PM?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the phrase sounds

blocks.note: a suppressed prime minister is a leader who has been banned

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister is described as a leader who was silenced, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British prime minister, which tempts a political answer, but a different Ted Heath led a famous British big band.
explanation.definitionFit: Ted Heath the musician directed his own dance orchestra from 1945, so he was the leader of a band.

clue.text: Minister's chatter cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short removes its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: to rabbit (on) is British slang for talk at length, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk

explanation.surface: A clergyman's long-winded talk gets interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister's' reads as possessive, but the 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader of a congregation, a minister of that faith.

clue.text: Mail a lad abroad about a spiritual leader

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so these letters are scattered into a new order
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone posts a letter overseas to a boy about a religious figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the chief spiritual teacher of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Increasing the wealth of church popular in Niger originally

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so the short pieces go within the rearranged word
the word is taken back to some earlier form, so its letters are put in a different order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange; Niger is a West African country
CH is the abbreviation for church
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A church that is popular in Niger is growing richer from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like a first-letters signal, but the whole of Niger is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich is to make richer, so enriching means adding to someone's wealth.

clue.text: Deadlock dad's locked in new semi

indicators.note: something locked in is shut inside, so one piece is held within the other
a new version is a remade one, so the word's letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange; a semi is a semi-detached house
pa is dad, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: Father is stuck in his newly built semi-detached house, a stalemate.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a situation in which no progress is possible, a standoff.

clue.text: Circles Ayr and gets disoriented

indicators.note: someone disoriented has lost their bearings, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: letters to rearrange; Ayr is a Scottish coastal town
more letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A visitor goes round and round Ayr, getting lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To gyrate is to move in a circle or spiral, so gyrates is a verb matching circles.

clue.text: Despicable person with dog

blocks.note: first meaning: a contemptible man, an old-fashioned insult
second meaning: a hunting dog

explanation.surface: A nasty character is out walking his dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Hound means both a dog bred for hunting and, dated, a scoundrel, much as dog itself does.

clue.text: New York politician plugging Ireland, say

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so one piece is stuffed inside the other

blocks.note: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland
MP is a Member of Parliament
to state is to say

explanation.surface: A New York politician is promoting Ireland, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York politician' reads as one phrase, but New York is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Empire State is the official nickname of New York State.

clue.text: Pretty fine tune

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A lovely little melody is being praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty fine' reads as 'quite good', but pretty is the definition and fine gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is a dated or poetic word for beautiful, as in fair maiden.

clue.text: Close to old and strange house

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: Near an old, peculiar dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Drum is old British slang for a house or flat, and rum means odd in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal and Cockney slang a drum is a dwelling, as in someone's place.

clue.text: On the subject of a rugby player, very large

blocks.note: taken as written
a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size

explanation.surface: Speaking of a huge rugby forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugby player' tempts PRO, but it is the position PROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos is a preposition meaning concerning or with reference to, from French à propos.

clue.text: Was obsequious to a degree, one visiting editor

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
D is short for degree, as in the qualification
the Roman numeral for one
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: Someone fawned excessively, calling on the newspaper's editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' reads as 'somewhat', but each word is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To toady is to flatter servilely in the hope of advantage, so toadied is past tense of being sycophantic.

clue.text: Pangs of conscience about son getting in again

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: re means concerning
more means additionally, once again
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent feels guilty about their son moving back in.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is deep regret for wrongdoing, which is the gnawing feeling of a troubled conscience.

clue.text: More demanding Irish novelist, by right

blocks.note: Laurence Sterne, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Ireland
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A tough Irish writer, standing by what is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterner is the comparative of stern, strict and exacting, so stricter or harder to satisfy.
